title: Time-of-day of combined chemoimmunotherapy as a prognostic factor in solid tumors
summary:
The body’s day–night rhythm influences many physiological processes – including the immune system and the way medications work. Recent studies suggest that the time of day at which a systemic cancer therapy is administered may have prognostic significance.
A research group led by Huang et al. (2025) found that patients with lung cancer (NSCLC) who received their chemo-immunotherapy in the morning had a longer overall survival than those treated in the afternoon. Our study aims to investigate whether this association can be demonstrated again.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name: Patients with solid tumors who received chemoimmunotherapy at the West German Cancer Center Essen. It is being evaluated whether the time of day of therapy administration is a prognostic factor.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Solid tumor, administration of chemoimmunotherapy
Exclusion criteria:
non-metastatic stage
